question: Which document and measurement contracts determine pages, and which layout authority can be removed or reused?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, frozen from status at fe0e9599a6 on 2026-10-04 (39 units), and judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was open as pursue-unbound at queue position 14. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: Plate applications install and import platejs, never plitejs, and every mounted Plate editable renders through Plate's plugin pipeline (VISION.md boundary law).
Pagination is view-owned derived geometry, not document truth; PagedEditable owns live layout, page surfaces and omission; measurePages stays the headless path.
Plate adds no pagination plugin, kit, store or second runtime and reuses the Plite PagedEditable.
Inside packages/platejs, only exact facade, proxy or intentional replacement leaves import plitejs.
Explicit page omission (virtualize) and exact-host usePageLayout keep working for Plate apps.
evidenceReuse: This review reused the 2026-09-15/16 pagination records, decision page and implementation plan for the Plite target, which live source confirms (no pageBreaks, useLayout or createPaginationDecorationRuntime; NodeFragmentationPlan union; PagedEditable props). It newly inspected Plate's EditorContent pipeline, the private PlateContentEditableContext, VirtualizedEditorContent, the Plate pagination facade, the entrypoint DAG and the public Plate pagination guide. The earlier review's Plate row considered only a plugin, kit or separate runtime, never the content-pipeline variant.
summary: The job is to render a Plate document as measured pages with custom chrome, fragmentation and optional page omission, with headless measurement for previews. Live Plite source matches the earlier Pursue. PagedEditable owns live layout and page omission, measurePages is one-shot, fragmentation is text, atomic or direct-children, and page-break authority is deleted. The remaining gap is at the Plate boundary. Plate renders plugin components only because EditorContent passes pipeRenderElement, pipeRenderLeaf, pipeRenderText, piped DOM handlers, shortcuts, slots and PlateRoot to the Plite editable. Its only way to swap the editable is a private override context that VirtualizedEditorContent uses. The platejs/pagination/react entry is an identity re-export of the raw component, and the DAG forbids it from importing Plate react-core, so no public path paginates with plugins. The public guide imports a nonexistent Plate component. The smallest fix keeps Plite unchanged and adds a Plate paged EditorContent variant through the existing private override context. A public hook that exposes piped renderers loses, and so does moving Plate's render pipeline into Plite.

callSites.current: import { PagedEditable } from 'platejs/pagination/react'; <EditorRoot editor={editor}><PagedEditable ref={editableRef} page={{ margins: 72, preset: 'letter' }} /></EditorRoot> renders the raw Plite editable with no Plate plugin renderers, handlers, shortcuts or slots (the guide imports a nonexistent Plate).
callSites.proposed: import { PagedEditorContent, usePageLayout } from 'platejs/pagination/react'; <EditorRoot editor={editor}><PagedEditorContent ref={editableRef} page={{ margins: 72, preset: 'letter' }} pageView={{ gap: 24, mode: 'single' }} renderPage={renderPage} virtualize /></EditorRoot>, implemented as EditorContent with the private editable override set to Plite PagedEditable. The raw PagedEditable stays in plitejs/pagination/react only. The name is Best API's call.

alternatives: Keeping the exact identity facade loses. Plate apps get raw element and leaf rendering with no plugin components, handlers, shortcuts, slots or PlateRoot binding, and the guide teaches it.

Changing the Plate facade wins. It replaces the raw PagedEditable re-export with a Plate paged EditorContent variant that mounts PagedEditable through EditorContent's private editable override, exactly like VirtualizedEditorContent. It is the smallest change, reuses the existing override, and adds no runtime.

Adding a public Plate hook that returns piped renderers and handlers for any raw editable loses. It leaks pipeline assembly (shortcuts, slots, PlateRoot, content attributes) into app code and creates a second composition path.

Merging variants into one EditorContent with a public component prop loses. Doctrine treats the dedicated component as the mounted-view lifetime boundary, and the prop types would not infer per variant.

Replacing the architecture by moving Plate's render pipeline into Plite, so any Plite editable renders installed plugins, loses on the hard law that Plite stays free of Plate product rendering policy.
Adding a Plate pagination plugin or kit loses because it has no independent job, as the prior review found.
proofLimits: This is a source review only, with no browser or package run. This review derived from source that a Plate plugin component fails to render inside raw PagedEditable (renderers are props that only EditorContent supplies) and did not observe it at runtime. Whether PagedEditable's own props (ref, scrollSelectionIntoView, decorationStore) compose cleanly with EditorContent's piped props is a design question, and so is the exact Plate name. The Plite pagination receipts (37 tests, cost packet, Chromium cases) are historical. docs/vision/plite.md carries an unrelated staged hunk.
